name: Scan — Did the Signed-Up Player Turn Up?
note: Not a gate. A gate is handed a feature and asks whether it clears the bar; the scan asks whether anyone entered the race. Every gate here was green while the ad service had no callers at all.

mutations.name: a screen calls a method that does not exist
mutations.why: The scan asks whether the players who signed up turned up. A renamed method leaves the call site pointing at nothing — it type-checks in no language here, passes every gate, and throws the first time a real person opens that screen.

mutations.name: a translation called with double quotes drops its placeholder
mutations.why: External audit V10. The scan read only single-quoted keys; t("...") fell through to 'dynamic', so the key looked unused and its placeholders were never checked. The same call with the param removed would print {time} to the player, and the scan said nothing.

mutations.name: params passed through something the scan cannot read (control)
mutations.why: External audit V10, the other half. t(key, params) passes whatever params holds, and the scan used to read it as passing nothing — a CONFIRMED defect for a call that works. The control keeps that from coming back: an unreadable second argument is reported as SUSPECT for a human, and CONFIRMED stays at 0.
